auth_method.description: Choose how to authenticate with the MQTT broker.
auth_method.title: Authentication

data_description.auth_url: The OIDC issuer URL of your identity provider (e.g. auth.example.com/realms/myrealm). Do not enter the full authorization endpoint — OIDC discovery handles this automatically.
data_description.client_id: The OAuth client ID registered at the identity provider. Must be a **public client** (no client secret). Default: `tc_iot_communicator`.

auth_url.description:
Enter the OIDC issuer URL of your identity provider (e.g. Keycloak, Azure AD, Auth0). The integration discovers the authorization and token endpoints automatically via /.well-known/openid-configuration.

The OAuth flow uses Authorization Code with PKCE (S256) — no client secret is needed. The redirect URI is: /auth/tc_iot/callback (relative to your HA base URL).
auth_url.title: OAuth / JWT login

data_description.password: The password configured on the MQTT broker.
data_description.username: The username configured on the MQTT broker.

credentials.description: Enter the username and password for your MQTT broker.
credentials.title: Broker credentials

obtain_token.description:
A browser window has opened for you to log in at the identity provider.

After login, the integration receives an authorization code and exchanges it for a **JWT access token** via PKCE. The JWT claims `preferred_username` (or `sub`) and `exp` are used to configure the MQTT connection.

This page updates automatically once authentication is complete.
obtain_token.title: Waiting for login

reauth_confirm.description:
The MQTT broker rejected the stored credentials or the JWT access token has expired (the `exp` claim is in the past). Enter the broker credentials again, or log in again at the identity provider to obtain a fresh token.

To avoid frequent re-authentication with OAuth, increase the **Access Token Lifespan** on your identity provider.
reauth_confirm.title: Re-authentication required
